For a 50-person Indian company, I’d take these three into the final procurement round. The key issue is that FCM and Thomas Cook are quote-based, so an apples-to-apples “total cost” requires a written commercial proposal.

Provider	Cost / value structure	Cancellation & flexibility	Support	Key trade-off
ITILITE	Travel plan starts ₹0/month, with no minimum commitment; one fixed trip fee covers booking, changes and support. 
Itilite
	Online cancellation/change; supplier fare rules still apply. ITILITE says modifications within the same trip have no extra service fee. 
Itilite
	24/7 human support; dedicated AM on higher tiers. 
Itilite
	Best cost transparency, but get the actual per-trip fee before signing.
FCM Travel	Custom quote; value comes from negotiated corporate rates. FCM advertises up to 38% hotel savings and 80,000+ prepaid Indian hotels. 
FCM Travel
	Flexible cancellation available on selected corporate hotel rates; booking-specific rules apply. 
FCM Travel
	Dedicated consultant + 24/7 support. 
FCM Travel
	Strong managed service, but pricing/fees aren't public.
Thomas Cook India	Custom quote; combines air, hotel, rail, car, visa, forex and MICE. 
Thomas Cook
	Supplier-specific; negotiate cancellation/refund handling in contract.	24/7 emergency desk, plus dedicated/implant servicing. 
Thomas Cook
	Broadest offline/managed-service coverage, but potentially heavier operational model.
Before paying, demand these 7 numbers

Domestic flight booking/service fee

International booking fee

Hotel booking fee/markup

Cancellation/change service fee

GST treatment + GST input-credit handling

24/7 support SLA and escalation time

Annual minimum commitment or implementation fee

My purchase shortlist: get written quotes from ITILITE + FCM + Thomas Cook using the same expected annual spend and booking volume. Don't compare headline discounts alone; compare all-in cost per trip after cancellations, GST recovery and support fees.
